title: Agent subprocess inherits full parent environment including API keys

finding.claim: Agent subprocess inherits full parent environment including API keys
finding.recommendation: Introduce an environment allow-list/scrubbing mechanism when constructing the child process environment, so that provider API keys and other secrets are not forwarded to third-party agent executables. Alternatively, document the intentional inheritance as an accepted operator trade-off with explicit opt-out.

code_region.note: region text is the finding's validated evidence quote; full region could not be re-located at the record head

refutation.quote: env = {n: os.environ[n] for n in names + extra if n in os.environ}
refutation.reason: The cited vulnerable line was removed. The current code constructs the child environment from an allow-list plus explicit opt-ins, rather than inheriting the full parent environment.

probe.summary: Providers-env probe (`probes/closingB_providers.py`, 536112b7d4dd section; providers.py:189-215, 316): the parent env carried OPENAI_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY / CODEREVIEW_TEST_SECRET / DUMP_PATH. The environment the agent process actually ran with had exactly 10 keys (CODEREVIEW_PROMPT, HOME, HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, LC_CTYPE, NO_PROXY, PATH, and the lowercase proxy spellings) — secret keys present: NONE. With the documented opt-in CODEREVIEW_AGENT_ENV=CODEREVIEW_TEST_SECRET, exactly that named variable appears and OPENAI_API_KEY remains absent: inheritance is per-variable and operator-chosen, never wholesale.
